solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Without serious intention heartless judge finds victim

parts.note: casual means offhand, not meant seriously

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle letter, so the centre of the judge word goes

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: Someone caught out by a flippant, uncaring judge ends up as the injured party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the R from the middle of TRY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty is a person killed or injured in an accident or war, i.e. a victim.

clue.text: Romeo entering small wood causes laugh on stage

indicators.note: entering means the Romeo letter goes inside the small wood

parts.note: a copse is a small group of trees
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo walking into a thicket gets an unintended laugh from the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' suggests the play, but it is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang, to corpse is to break into uncontrollable laughter during a performance.

clue.text: Singular boast about keeping figure in field

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
keeping means care, as in 'in someone's keeping'
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: A unique boast about having charge of a figure out in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' works as in 'crow about care': the boast concerns the keeping, which is named first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a human-shaped dummy set up in a field to frighten birds.

clue.text: Boost to have soldiers relieving us in some 31 days?

indicators.note: relieving means the soldiers take over the post held by us, as a relief guard does

parts.note: August is one of the months with 31 days
men means soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Soldiers taking our place to boost things in a month of 31 days.
explanation.walkthrough: In AUGUST, MEN replaces the US.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase or enlarge something, i.e. to boost it.

clue.text: With duke sent down, now one grovels

indicators.note: sent down means the duke letter moves lower in this down entry

parts.note: today means now, nowadays

explanation.surface: A duke has been jailed, so now somebody is crawling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent down' (British for jailed) moves the D of TODAY one place down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a sycophant who flatters and fawns, someone who grovels to superiors.

clue.text: Officials ultimately do nothing to hide European corruption

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word officials
to hide means the do-nothing word wraps round and conceals the European letter

parts.note: to laze is to do nothing

explanation.surface: Officials who idle around and cover up for a European are a picture of corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleaze is sordid dishonesty, especially bribery and scandal in public life.

clue.text: University with nuclear research facility in the French city

indicators.note: in means the university and facility letters go inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
CERN is the particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: A university with a nuclear laboratory in some French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a city in central Switzerland, on Lake Lucerne.

clue.text: Coordinate a policy broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the words are spoken aloud on air, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A political party coordinating a policy for broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to arrange them in order or bring them into agreement, to coordinate them.

clue.text: Intellectual way to stop foreign article being duplicated

indicators.note: to stop means the way letters plug the gap between the two articles

parts.note: ein is the German indefinite article, a or an
being duplicated means the foreign article appears a second time
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A clever path to prevent a foreign word appearing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: ST goes between the two EINs.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein's name is used for any genius, a great intellectual.

clue.text: Unconventional people not paired at dances

parts.note: odd means unpaired, as an odd sock
balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: Eccentrics who turn up at dances without partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddballs are eccentric people whose behaviour is strange or unorthodox.

clue.text: Stand to ease pressure on back?

definitions.text: Stand to ease pressure on back?

parts.words: Stand to ease pressure on back?
parts.note: reads like a support for a sore back, but describes a military defence mounted by troops at the rear of a retreating army

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a posture aid for back pain; in fact the 'stand' is a defensive fight and the 'back' is the rear of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is a defensive fight by the rear of a retreating force, protecting the troops in front.

clue.text: Shady borders round church close lacking a background

indicators.note: round means the outer letters are wrapped around what follows
the borders of a word are its first and last letters, here of shady

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: lacking means the word for close goes without the a printed next to it

parts.note: near means close by

explanation.surface: A description of a shaded garden edge round a church with something missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close lacking a' is a trimmed synonym: drop the A from the word for close, not from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery is the painted backdrop of a stage set, the background behind the action.

clue.text: Titled fellow from circle in London borough

indicators.note: the circle letter comes from within the borough's name, so it sits inside it

parts.note: Barnet is a borough of north London
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A titled man hailing from a ring of a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is a London borough; the circle O goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary title ranking below a baron, so is a titled man.

clue.text: Reviewer a layman initially on the danger list?

parts.note: a critic reviews books, plays and films

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of layman

explanation.surface: Asks whether a reviewer who is only an amateur deserves to be on a list of dangers.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient in critical condition is seriously ill, which hospitals call being on the danger list.

clue.text: Retreat after slaughter associated with old battle

indicators.note: after means the retreat word comes behind the others

parts.note: a cull is the selective slaughter of animals
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: An army pulled back after a massacre linked to an old battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Culloden (1746) was the last pitched battle on British soil, ending the Jacobite rising.

clue.text: Bug found in green sauce Penny refused

parts.note: eco- means environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: refused means the penny letter is turned away, removed from the sauce word

parts.note: lip means sauce, cheek or insolence

explanation.surface: A germ is discovered in a green sauce that someone wouldn't pay for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green sauce' looks like pesto or salsa verde, but the two words split apart; 'sauce' here is cheek, as in 'none of your lip'.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium, and a bug is everyday slang for a germ or infection.

clue.text: Gold box Rubbra emptied for ensemble

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a chest is a large box

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of Rubbra is removed, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A gold box once belonging to the composer Rubbra was cleared out for a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Rubbra was an English composer, fitting the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Hidden crop covered with fresh seed

indicators.note: covered with means the crop word is enclosed by the reworked seed letters
fresh signals that the letters of seed take a new arrangement

parts.note: to clip is to crop, as hair

explanation.surface: A crop that's out of sight because it is covered by new seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' could look like a hidden-word signal, but it is the definition, in the past-participle sense of obscured.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclipsed means obscured or blocked from view, so hidden.

clue.text: Cringe — or one to make you do so?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shrink back in fear

definitions.text: one to make you do so?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: one who cows you

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented: someone who cows another would be a 'cow-er', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch in fear, and a person who intimidates or cows others could jokingly be called that.

clue.text: This writer has to support others unwilling to accept control?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits beneath, so it follows the others word

parts.note: the rest are the others
the setter would say I've, I have

explanation.surface: The setter has to prop up others who resist discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive describes a person or horse that is restless and resists being controlled.

clue.text: Feel so bad catching a cold, be humiliated

indicators.note: catching means the jumbled letters take in the a and cold letters
bad signals that the letters of feel so go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone feels rotten after catching a cold, and is embarrassed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges FEEL SO to LOSEFE, and 'catching' puts A plus C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose face is an idiom for losing respect or standing, being humiliated in front of others.

clue.text: Bomb vessel in front part

indicators.note: in means the vessel goes inside the front part

parts.note: fore is the front part, as of a ship
a tun is a large cask, a vessel

explanation.surface: A bomb planted in a ship's bows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bomb' is British slang for a lot of money: 'it cost a bomb'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune and a bomb are both informal terms for a very large amount of money.

clue.text: Design ultimately graceful clothes having turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top
clothes means the two words wrap around and conceal the letters

explanation.surface: A design that, in the end, makes graceful clothes after they've been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits reversed across the end of 'ultimately' and the start of 'graceful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is a diamond-check knitting pattern, a design seen on socks and sweaters.

clue.text: Current doctor to protect by putting on thick coat

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: to protect means the doctor letters surround and shield the word for by

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
past means by, as in walking past or by

explanation.surface: A doctor shielding a current flow by applying a heavy layer of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the painting technique of laying on paint thickly so brush or knife marks remain.

clue.text: Forest creature threatened with old man circling

indicators.note: circling means the old man letters go round the with word

parts.note: pa is father, the old man
and means with, together

explanation.surface: An endangered woodland animal surrounded by an elderly man.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda lives in bamboo forests and is a famously vulnerable species.

clue.text: Terror seen around the world makes one hesitate

indicators.note: around means the terror word is placed about the world word

parts.note: fear means terror
an orb is a sphere, the globe or world

explanation.surface: Fear spread across the world makes people pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back or refrain from doing something, which is to hesitate.

clue.text: Jumping gun stops motor racing in kingdom

indicators.note: stops means the reworked gun letters plug the motor racing letters

parts.note: F1, written FI, is Formula One motor racing

indicators.note: jumping signals that the letters of gun leap about into a new order

explanation.surface: A jumped gun halts a Grand Prix start in some kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is written with the digit 1 read as the letter I; 'kingdom' is the biological rank, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungi form their own kingdom in biological classification, alongside plants and animals.

clue.text: High-technology business not suited to setting?

definitions.text: High-technology business not suited to setting?

parts.words: High-technology business not suited to setting?
parts.note: a new, fast-growing tech sector is named after the dawn, which is the opposite of the sun going down

explanation.walkthrough: The joke: something named after the sun coming up would hardly fit with the sun going down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunrise industry is a new, rapidly growing sector such as electronics or high technology.

clue.text: Main charity sent back something sparkling

indicators.note: sent back means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean, the main being the sea
aid means charitable help

explanation.surface: Charity aid shipped home across the sea sparkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the old word for the sea; here it is the Mediterranean, MED.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled crown or headband, which glitters.

clue.text: Large one supplied with carpet that's free

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
I is the Roman numeral for one
to carpet someone is to give them a dressing-down, to berate them

explanation.surface: A big item that comes with a carpet included at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is a verb: to carpet is to reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set free, so as verbs the two are synonyms.
